Please answer: After cutting the efferent nerve that innervates the left hind limb of the spinal frog (see figure), if end A is stimulated immediately, can contraction activity of the left hind limb be seen?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Using a frog whose brain has been removed but whose spinal cord is retained (called a spinal frog) as the material, carry out a reflex activity experiment. Please answer: after cutting the efferent nerve that innervates the left hind limb of the spinal frog (see figure), if end A is stimulated immediately, can contraction activity of the left hind limb be seen?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is labeled “nerve center,” and “afferent nerve” and “efferent nerve” are drawn. The efferent nerve leads from the nerve center toward the effector direction of the left hind limb, and is cut at a place near the left side; the left side of the cut is labeled end A, and the right side is labeled end B. It can be seen from the figure that end A is the end that is still connected to the left hind limb muscle after being cut, and end B is the end that is still connected to the nerve center. Then reason: the efferent nerve belongs to motor nerves, and its function is to transmit nerve impulses to the effector muscle. After cutting the efferent nerve, although end A has already been disconnected from the spinal cord nerve center, it is still connected to the left hind limb muscle. Immediately stimulating end A can excite this segment of efferent nerve and transmit the excitation to the left hind limb muscle, causing muscle contraction. Therefore, contraction activity of the left hind limb can be seen.
